title: refactor(dedicated-autoscaler): unify burst controls and utilization reporting path
author: Marina Patel
description:
Motivation: our dedicated autoscaler had two parallel code paths for burst controls (token-bucket smoothing) and utilization reporting that caused duplication, inconsistent metrics, and occasional double-accounting of burst capacity when backpressure and priority routing were enabled. This PR refactors the autoscaler to unify the burst control execution path with the utilization reporting pipeline so that: 1) a single source of truth computes available burst tokens and effective throughput guarantees; 2) utilization and queueing metrics are emitted consistently; 3) SLO handoffs (throughput guarantees -> throttling decisions) respect priority routing and canary policies.

What changed (high level): unified token-bucket implementation moved from autoscaler/core to autoscaler/engine; added a lightweight adapter for priority routing to query the same burst state; consolidated utilization reporters into a single producer that emits per-fleet, per-model and per-priority metrics (util_pct, burst_tokens, queued_requests, effective_tput) and a pre-aggregated daily time-series for billing. Introduced smoothing window config and improved backlog accounting to avoid transient spikes causing capacity overcommit.

Compatibility & migration: config keys were renamed under dedicated.autoscaler.burst -> dedicated.autoscaler.burst_control (backwards-compatible aliases are provided; a small migration job rewrites old persisted bucket states on startup when the cluster flag autoscaler.migrate_burst_state is set). Users of internal token inspection APIs should use the new AutoscalerClient.getBurstState endpoint.

Testing & verification: unit tests for new token-bucket correctness, integration tests with priority routing and canary policies, e2e perf job validating 99th pct latency under handicapped GPU availability. CI runs included: unit, integration, e2e perf; observed a flaky test in e2e (fixed in subsequent commit). Metrics validated in staging by comparing pre/post reports across 48h of traffic.
